My land is about 6 mu total, split between my main fields and a small plot near the house. I've been farming this same land since I married into this village forty years ago. My husband is gone now, and my son works in Handan city, so I work the fields myself with help from my daughter-in-law during busy seasons.

I know one thing well: wheat and corn. That is what everyone here grows. That is what the soil knows. I will do the wheat-corn rotation on my 5 main mu — plant wheat in October, harvest in June, then immediately plant corn in the same fields, harvest in September. I have done this my whole life.

On the 1 mu near the house I will plant garlic in the autumn like always. I sell some in the market and keep some to eat.

For seeds, I buy improved wheat seed from the village supply station — they told me Kenong 199 is good, and my neighbor uses it. For corn I always buy hybrid seed, the yellow kind in the red bag, same as last year. For garlic I keep my own seed from last year's harvest.

For fertilizer I put down what my neighbor puts down. We apply compound fertilizer before planting and then urea top-dressing when the plants are growing. Wheat needs more water — I will irrigate before winter sets in, then again when it joints, then when it heads, then once more when the grain is filling. Four times total. Corn needs less — just when it is dry in the critical periods, maybe twice.

I spray pesticide twice on wheat for aphids and powdery mildew. Twice on corn too, mostly for armyworm.
